findings.title: Tool requests or reads secrets / environment variables
findings.recommendation: A tool has no business holding your keys. A server that takes a secret as a parameter is either badly designed or harvesting credentials. Never pass secrets in tool arguments; let the host process read them from its own environment, and only for servers you trust.

findings.title: Tool executes arbitrary commands
findings.recommendation: Not hostile by itself; shell tools are legitimate. But they should never reach an agent without a sandbox, a command allowlist and human confirmation on each invocation.

findings.title: Tool makes network requests to arbitrary addresses
findings.recommendation: Constrain egress with a domain allowlist at the host network layer. Asking the model nicely in a prompt is not a control.

findings.title: Description contains an external endpoint and/or an instruction to send data
findings.recommendation: Check where the data goes. If a tool sends results to an external URL that URL is an exfiltration channel. Allow only an explicit domain allowlist.

findings.title: Tool references another tool (list_practice_stacks)
findings.evidence: description excerpt: "Return one WealthMCP Practice Stack: the MCP servers that make up the workflow plus the starter prompts written for it. Use list_practice_stacks first to get a valid stack id. {'readOnlyHint': True, 'idempotentHint': True, 'openWorldHint': False}"
findings.recommendation: Check the context of the mention. Cross-references between tools are fine in documentation, not as directives to the agent.

findings.title: Tool references another tool (list_skills)
findings.evidence: description excerpt: "Return one guided workflow's full instructions and guardrails. Use list_skills first for a valid slug. Follow the skill exactly; never improvise from the blurb. {'readOnlyHint': True, 'idempotentHint': True, 'openWorldHint': False}"
findings.recommendation: Check the context of the mention. Cross-references between tools are fine in documentation, not as directives to the agent.

findings.title: Tool references another tool (get_skill)
findings.evidence: description excerpt: "List the guided workflows (skills) this server ships. Load one with get_skill(slug) and follow it before answering a composition request from the raw tools alone. {'readOnlyHint': True, 'idempotentHint': True, 'openWorldHint': False}"
findings.recommendation: Check the context of the mention. Cross-references between tools are fine in documentation, not as directives to the agent.
